title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page): S is a base scheme, G an S-group scheme and g ∈ G(S) a section, presumably unipotent. One looks for a homomorphism of S-group schemes φ: G_{a,S} → G with (4) φ(1) = g, i.e. a one-parameter additive subgroup through g, an 'exponential' t ↦ g^t. Over a field of characteristic 0 such a φ is unique when it exists. Faithfully flat descent then makes existence local for the fpqc topology. In characteristic p uniqueness fails, because there are nontrivial additive endomorphisms such as x ↦ x^p − x that kill 1.

This page: Grothendieck restricts to a noetherian integral S whose generic point y has characteristic 0 (mixed characteristic, e.g. S = Spec Z or a ring of integers).
(i) By the field case at y and a spreading-out (limit) argument, there is a nonempty open U ⊂ S and φ_U: G_a|U → G|U satisfying (4) on U (the manuscript writes G|U → G|U, a slip). For fixed U this φ_U is unique.
(ii) By uniqueness, the φ_U glue, so there is a largest open U on which φ exists. The question becomes whether necessarily U = S.
(iii) Suppose U ≠ S. Localize at a maximal (generic) point x of the closed set S∖U. In Spec O_{S,x} the bad locus is only the closed point. So it suffices to show that for S local with closed point s, φ_U extends over all of S. Such an extension spreads out to a neighbourhood of x, contradicting maximality.
(iv) In the case of interest S is regular of dimension 1, so the local schemes are traits (spectra of DVRs of mixed characteristic (0,p)). He announces he will restrict to this 'crucial' case.

The next page treats the trait: take the schematic closure L of φ_y(G_{a,y}). He notes the special fibre (L^0)_s need not be reduced and φ_s need not be a monomorphism. He then tests G = GL(M) with φ_y(λ) = exp(λX) = Σ X^i λ^i / i!, X = log g. Over a trait with residue characteristic p this is integral only under restrictive conditions on X (e.g. X^p = 0 and integrality of X^i/i!). So the expected answer is 'not always'. The purpose is to construct canonical one-parameter (G_a-) subgroups through unipotent elements over arithmetic bases. In the context of the Longue Marche this is presumably related to unipotent monodromy, e.g. Dehn-twist-like elements; the first line possibly mentions a 'lacet', but this is uncertain.
errors: φ_U is written as G|U → G|U; it should be G_a|U → G|U (a slip).
The 'existence of a nonempty open U' tacitly requires G of finite presentation over S and the standard limit argument; it is not stated.

The reduction is sound, but the question U = S has a generally negative answer in mixed characteristic. For example, a regular unipotent element (Jordan block of size > p) in GL_n over Z_(p) has no G_a-homomorphism through it, since exp(λX) is not integral. The page itself does not yet claim either way; the next page starts to see the obstruction.

ideas.what: Uniqueness of one-parameter subgroups through a unipotent element in characteristic 0 implies gluing, hence a largest open of definition of φ.
ideas.modern_name: Extension of homomorphisms from the generic fibre; largest open of definition via uniqueness and descent
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (EGA IV limit and spreading-out techniques)
ideas.where_published: EGA IV §8 (limits), SGA 3 (group schemes) for the techniques

ideas.what: Reduction of an extension problem to a local scheme at a maximal point of the bad locus, and in dimension 1 to a trait.
ideas.modern_name: Noetherian induction / localization at generic points of the complement

ideas.what: Problem: given unipotent g ∈ G(S) over a mixed-characteristic base, does the characteristic-0 exponential t ↦ g^t extend to a homomorphism G_{a,S} → G?
ideas.modern_name: Integral exponentials / Springer-type maps and 'saturation' of unipotent elements over Z_(p)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre (saturation, exponents p, 1990s); Seitz (good A1 subgroups); Deligne (2014, semisimplicity of tensor products in char p); Balaji–Deligne–Parameswaran

missed.claim: Grothendieck poses, in an anabelian/Teichmüller context, the problem of extending the characteristic-0 one-parameter subgroup through a unipotent element over a mixed-characteristic trait. This is essentially the integrality question for exponentials later studied by Serre, Seitz and Deligne (exp(tX) over Z_(p), saturation, nilpotency order < p). It is an anticipation of the question rather than a result.
missed.quote: la question revient à voir si on a nécessairement U = S ... en localisant on trouve un trait
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is minor historical interest. It shows Grothendieck meeting the 'exponential over Z_(p)' obstruction in connection with unipotent elements (possibly monodromy). No new result appears on this page.

deep.surprise_reason: The page carries out a standard EGA-style reduction (uniqueness, largest open, localize to a trait) for the extension of G_a-subgroups through unipotent sections. The only interest is the early framing of a problem later studied by Serre and Deligne, but nothing is finished here.
